title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. k is a commutative ring and L. is a '½-simplicial' k-module. In context this is a simplicial or semi-simplicial k-module in the Dold–Kan/Dold–Puppe setting. L^! denotes the associated normalized (Dold–Puppe) chain complex. Phi and Psi are two basic simplicial abelian groups.
- Phi_n is free of rank n+1. Its normalized complex is presumably the contractible complex Z -> Z in degrees 1, 0.
- Psi_n is free of rank n. It is presumably Phi modulo the constants, a model of K(Z,1).
- The index ranges on this page fit these ranks: Lambda^i Phi_n is nonzero exactly for i <= n+1, and Lambda^j Psi_n exactly for j <= n.
- By the décalage formulas of Dold–Puppe/Illusie, Lambda^j Psi has normalized complex Z[j]. Lambda^i Phi has normalized complex (Z -> Z) in degrees i, i-1.

The previous page (Prop. 1) classifies the L. whose components L_n and homotopy groups are projective. These are exactly the products of Lambda^i Phi_k ⊗ M_i (i >= 1) and Lambda^j Psi_k ⊗ N_j (j >= 0). Equivalently, L^! is a product of elementary complexes (M_i -> M_i) in degrees i, i-1 and N_j in degree j. Here N_j = H_j and M_i = B_{i-1}.

This page:
- Cor. 1: one may add 'of finite type' throughout. L_n is f.t. iff the L^n are f.t. iff all M_i and N_j are f.t. The explicit levelwise formula is L_n = prod_{1<=i<=n+1} Lambda^i Phi_{n,k} ⊗ M_i × prod_{0<=j<=n} Lambda^j Psi_{n,k} ⊗ N_j.
- Cor. 2: L^! is of bounded degree iff only finitely many M_i and N_j are nonzero.
- Definition: L. is called 'spécial' when L^! is bounded, with f.t. projective components and f.t. projective homology. Equivalently, L. is isomorphic to a finite direct sum of the basic pieces Lambda^i Phi_k ⊗ M_i and Lambda^j Psi_k ⊗ N_j, with M_i and N_j projective of f.t. It is 'strictement spécial' if moreover the M_i and N_j are free.

Purpose: this sets up a class of simplicial models of perfect complexes with split homology. The next page shows this class is stable under ⊗ and under Lambda^i, Gamma^i, Sym^i (via Künneth/Eilenberg–Zilber), and reduces the strict case to models over Z. The aim is a dévissage for multiplicative/λ-structures on perfect complexes, presumably related to determinants or λ-operations in K-theory.
errors: In the definition of 'spécial' the exponent is written Lambda^j Phi_k ⊗ M_i; it should be Lambda^i Phi_k ⊗ M_i.
The second family is written Lambda^j Psi ⊗ M_j; it should be Lambda^j Psi ⊗ N_j.
The levelwise formula omits the exponent j on Lambda Psi_n and the lower bound j >= 0. Both are minor slips.
The phrase 'isomorphe à facteur direct de' is slightly loose. From Prop. 1, 'isomorphic to a finite direct sum (= product)' is what is meant.

ideas.what: Classification of simplicial modules with projective components and projective homotopy as products of elementary pieces Lambda^i Phi ⊗ M_i, Lambda^j Psi ⊗ N_j (finite-type and bounded variants)
ideas.modern_name: Dold–Kan correspondence applied to split complexes with projective homology; décalage Lambda^j(Z[1]) = Z[j]
ideas.usually_credited_to: Dold–Kan (1958), Dold–Puppe (1961); décalage formulas Illusie (Complexe cotangent, 1971)
ideas.where_published: Not in Grothendieck's published texts as far as known; the framework is Dold–Puppe/Illusie

ideas.what: Notion of 'special' / 'strictly special' simplicial modules as finite-type, bounded, homologically split simplicial models of perfect complexes, to be shown stable under ⊗, Lambda^i, Gamma^i, Sym^i
ideas.modern_name: Simplicial models of perfect complexes with split homology; polynomial functors on perfect complexes via Dold–Puppe

deep.surprise_reason: The page consists of routine corollaries of a Dold–Kan-type classification plus a definition. The interesting multiplicative and λ-structure material lies on later pages.
transcription_corrections: 'Gardons[?] ces notations' is plausible for the inserted phrase replacing 'Dans ces conditions'.
'On utilise[?] [-les-] L. ... si' should read roughly 'On appellera L. [parfait →] spécial si'. The word 'spéciaux/spécial' replaces the struck 'parfait'.
'modules en G[?] formés[?]' is likely 'de modules de la forme'.
'Lambda^j Phi_k ⊗ M_i' should read Lambda^i Phi_k ⊗ M_i, and 'Lambda^j Psi_k ⊗ M_j' should read ⊗ N_j.
In Cor. 1 the index under the second product is 0 <= j <= n.
